questiondescription.text:
Vectors: resultant displacement of a walk

Grade 12 CBE Essential 2.2: Write the resultant displacement of a walk of three or four legs as a column vector and find the distance walked.

Essential

This question is adapted from Question A10 in Section A of Chapter 29 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Foundation 1 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2006: new numbers, Kenyan context, STACK randomisation, a multi-leg walk with a resultant column vector, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: You added every leg as positive. West and south moves are negative.
The top number is the east to west move and the bottom number the north to south move.
Your vector goes from the finish back to G. The displacement goes from G to the finish.

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="zct"]]Your top number is right. For the bottom number add the north to south moves, with south negative.[[else]][[if test="zcb"]]Your bottom number is right. For the top number add the east to west moves, with west negative.[[else]]Add the east to west moves (west negative) for the top number and the north to south moves (south negative) for the bottom number.[[/if]][[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is the walk needed to go straight back along the grid. The distance walked adds every leg.

falsefeedback.text: Add the lengths of all the legs.
